CS101.title: Week 1 - Variables and Data Types
CS101.description: Write a program that demonstrates the use of variables, constants, and primitive data types in Java. Include at least one example of each primitive type.

CS101.title: Week 2 - Control Flow Statements
CS101.description: Implement a program that uses if-else, switch, and loops to solve a problem of your choice. Ensure all control flow structures are used appropriately.

CS101.title: Week 3 - Functions and Methods
CS101.description: Create a library of utility functions covering mathematical operations, string manipulation, and array processing.

submission.note: I have completed all the required functions. Please check my array sorting implementation.

CS101.title: Week 4 - Arrays and ArrayLists
CS101.description: Develop a student grade management system that uses arrays and ArrayLists to store, sort, and analyze student grades.

grade.feedback: Good work! Your sorting algorithm is efficient. Deducted points for missing edge case handling in empty array scenario.

CS101.title: Midterm Project - Simple Banking App
CS101.description: Design and implement a simple banking application that supports account creation, deposits, withdrawals, and transaction history using OOP principles.

grade.feedback: Excellent project! The code is well-structured and documented. Some room for improvement in exception handling. Overall very solid work.

MATH201.title: Problem Set 1 - Matrix Operations
MATH201.description: Solve the attached set of problems on matrix addition, multiplication, determinants, and inverses. Show all steps clearly.

MATH201.title: Problem Set 2 - Vector Spaces
MATH201.description: Complete problems on vector spaces, subspaces, linear independence, and basis. Submit handwritten or typed solutions.

MATH201.title: Problem Set 3 - Eigenvalues
MATH201.description: Solve eigenvalue and eigenvector problems. Include applications to diagonalization and matrix powers.

MATH201.title: Problem Set 4 - Linear Transformations
MATH201.description: Model real-world scenarios using linear transformations. Submit both theoretical derivations and computational implementations.

grade.feedback: Very good understanding of concepts. Lost a few points on the computational part due to minor errors in matrix multiplication.

PHYS101.title: Lab Report 1 - Kinematics
PHYS101.description: Write a full lab report on the kinematics experiment. Include raw data, analysis, graphs, and conclusion.

PHYS101.title: Problem Set - Newton's Laws
PHYS101.description: Solve 10 problems on Newton's laws of motion. Include free-body diagrams for each problem.

PHYS101.title: Lab Report 2 - Energy Conservation
PHYS101.description: Write a comprehensive lab report on the conservation of mechanical energy experiment with detailed error analysis.

grade.feedback: Excellent lab report! Great data analysis and error propagation. Minor formatting issues in the graphs section.

ENG101.title: Essay 1 - Argumentative Writing
ENG101.description: Write a 1000-word argumentative essay on a topic of your choice. Must include a clear thesis, supporting evidence, and counterargument.

ENG101.title: Research Paper Outline
ENG101.description: Submit a detailed outline for your final research paper including thesis statement, main arguments, and preliminary bibliography.

submission.note: Please let me know if the scope is appropriate before I proceed with the full paper.

ENG101.title: Final Research Paper
ENG101.description: Submit your final 3000-word research paper with proper citations in MLA format.

grade.feedback: Well-researched paper with strong arguments. The conclusion could be more developed. Some citations need formatting corrections.
